title: Fifa staff asked to attend interviews as Infantino sell-off scheme investigated
summary: Democrats to examine Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal Infantino could be subpoenaed to give evidence A number of past and present Fifa employees have received letters requesting they attend interviews for a congressional investigation into the global governing body sparked by the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal. Letters were sent on Wednesday to a number of staff along with a handful of former employees who held senior positions. They have been asked by Democrats on the House judiciary committee to give evidence as efforts gather pace to examine Gianni Infantino’s failed FFE scheme along with links between Fifa and the Trump administration. Continue reading...

title: Can Elon Musk really put AI datacentres in space? - The Latest
summary: The Trump administration has approved Elon Musk’s plan to create datacentres in space. US federal regulators have authorised the launch of one million Starmind orbital satellites, which are built by Musk’s SpaceX, to process data in space. Supporters argue the project will be more energy-efficient and reduce the environmental impact of datacentres on Earth as the AI industry grows. But how realistic is the plan and what could the consequences be? Michael Safi speaks to Guardian global technology editor Dan Milmo Continue reading...

title: Human flamethrower Aaron Rodgers lays bare the cultural rot at the once-great Steelers
summary: The quarterback’s spectacularly messy exit from Pittsburgh could herald an overdue collapse at one of the NFL’s most famous franchises Nobody in the world, except maybe Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II, is surprised that the franchise’s marriage of convenience with Aaron Rodgers ended in spectacular flames . Despite their own elevated idea of themselves, Pittsburgh have been one of the NFL’s messiest soap operas for a solid decade. When they linked up with the league’s messiest quarterback, it seemed certain we would get … even more mess. When they doubled down last offseason by hiring the coach with whom Rodgers had fallen out in Green Bay in the late 2010s, the mess became inevitable. We’d seen hints of the approaching drama in the season’s first 11 weeks. “What the fuck … call it!” Rodgers yelled at McCarthy as he looked for a play in early October. Continue reading...

title: Campbell Wright becomes first American to win World Cup biathlon event
summary: Wright delivers ‘best performance’ in Kontiolahti, Finland 24-year-old was actually born in New Zealand Campbell Wright made history on Thursday by becoming the first American to win a World Cup biathlon event. The 24-year-old was flawless at the shooting range in the World Cup opener in Kontiolahti , Finland and triumphed in the 20km individual race in 24 minutes and 29.8 seconds. Germany’s Justus Strelow finished 1:20 behind and Norway’s Vetle Sjaastad Christiansen was 1:23 adrift in third. Christiansen’s teammate, and last year’s World Cup overall champion, Sturla Holm Laegreid had to settle for fourth. Continue reading...

title: Steelers owner backs Mike McCarthy and attacks Aaron Rodgers’s ‘insubordination’
summary: Art Rooney II has ‘100% confidence’ in head coach Insists QB’s outbursts could not be tolerated The Pittsburgh Steelers owner and president, Art Rooney II, has provided his full support to head coach, Mike McCarthy, in his stunning fallout with Aaron Rodgers, and described the quarterback’s actions as “insubordination”. Rodgers was ⁠benched on Tuesday night and waived the following day after he accused McCarthy of falling asleep during a meeting in an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show. Rodgers said McCarthy missed meetings and a ⁠walkthrough later that same week – ⁠claims that were corroborated ​by unnamed sources in a report by ESPN on Wednesday. The Steelers are preparing to face the Denver Broncos on Friday with Mason ⁠Rudolph at quarterback. Continue reading...

title: ‘These families will be essentially homeless’: Flatbush groups condemn response to building collapse
summary: Advocacy groups say displaced families were sent to ‘subpar hotels’ until 30 November, with no housing plans in place afterward Flatbush community leaders are in an uproar on behalf of those who have been displaced in the aftermath of an apartment building collapse in Brooklyn earlier this month. They say some displaced tenants are in hotels until 30 November, but have no housing plans after that date. Advocacy groups said that those who were displaced were sent to “subpar hotels” that were also home to roaches and mice. Stays were only set for up to four days, leaving community leaders to push for longer stays. Continue reading...

title: Georgia judge blocks own order to turn over US election ballot copies to state board
summary: Superior court judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe paused the order after county election officials filed a notice of appeal A judge in Fulton county, Georgia , has blocked her own order to turn over electronic copies of 2020 election ballots seized by the FBI in a raid to the Georgia state election board. Superior court judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe paused the order after county election officials filed a notice of appeal. Continue reading...

title: US army calls detonation of bomb chemicals in Iowa a success after fears of toxic plume
summary: The army blows up US stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used for explosives, to avoid uncontrollable explosion The US army blew up the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used to make explosives, saying the first checks show Wednesday’s controlled detonation in Iowa didn’t spread toxic dust to nearby homes and farms. Earthen barriers were put up and foam and water were poured onto a pair of bunkers holding the 5 tons (4,500kg) of lead azide, and officials said those measures appear to have absorbed much of the blast. Continue reading...

title: US Senate ‘permitting bill’ threatens clean water protections to speed up energy projects
summary: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act passed the Senate and is now being debated in the House An industry-backed “permitting bill” approved by the US Senate would gut key clean water protections with changes that would do little to speed up the development of major energy projects, advocates warn. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (Baaja) passed the Senate 62-33 and is now being debated in the House. The Baaja is a “permitting reform” bill that aims to reduce the time it takes federal agencies to approve major energy and infrastructure projects, like power lines, fossil fuel pipelines, natural gas plants and datacenters . Continue reading...

title: Storms across US disrupt travel and force Thanksgiving parade cancellations
summary: Macy’s parade in New York postponed for first time ever as thousands across US north-east face power outages Heavy rain, winds, flooding and high tides crossed holiday plans across the US on Thursday, prompting the cancellations of at least two commercial Thanksgiving parades. A severe winter storm brought foul weather up and down the east coast, causing flooding, widespread power outages and even tornado warnings in several states. On the west coast, record high tides brought coastal flooding to several cities. And winter storm warnings were posted for several parts of the midwest. Continue reading...
authors: Edward Helmore , Keely Aouga and agencies

title: Strobe Talbott, Time magazine reporter and deputy US secretary of state, dies aged 80
summary: After 21 years at Time, Talbott joined the Clinton administration and later headed the Brookings Institution Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80. His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed he died peacefully after a long illness in his East Hampton, New York, home. Continue reading...

title: Trump alleges ‘fake’ economic figures released before US midterms but doesn’t provide evidence
summary: In a Thanksgiving post, the US president seeks investigation after blue wave of Democrats unseat Republicans Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party. In a holiday message on social media tinged with bitterness, the US president wished a happy thanksgiving “to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%”. Continue reading...

title: Father dies while trying to save teen son on icy California mountain hike
summary: Guillermo Batres was helping his son, who had slid down a hill and was clinging on to a tree, when he lost his footing A 44-year-old man who was trying to help his son navigate an icy patch of a southern California mountain trail slipped and fell roughly 500ft to his death, according to local authorities. Guillermo Batres, an avid hiker, set off on Sunday morning to summit Mount Baden-Powell in the San Gabriel mountains with his teenage son, according to Steve De Jong, a lieutenant with the Los Angeles county sheriff’s department. Continue reading...
